raw_goal: Build a dashboard for support risk.
enterprise_goal: Build an internal support-risk command center that lets support leads find aging, blocked, and overloaded queues before SLA breach.

primary_user.pain: Queue risk is discovered through manual spreadsheet checks after work is already late.
primary_user.success_moment: The lead opens the dashboard and sees the next three cases to unblock in under two minutes.

owner_or_buyer.decision_metric: Weekly aging-case count drops by 30 percent without adding coordinator headcount.

job_map.job: Review operational queue risk each morning
job_map.current_workaround: Export tickets to a spreadsheet and manually sort by age, owner, and blocker.
job_map.desired_outcome: Start the daily review from a trusted view of aging, blocked, and overloaded work.

artifact_map.purpose: Show aging, blocked, and overloaded queues in one decision view.
artifact_map.done_when: A lead can identify the top three unblock actions from seeded demo data.

artifact_map.purpose: Prove queue risk calculations and empty, loading, and error states.
artifact_map.done_when: Automated checks cover risk logic plus browser proof for the main route.

acceptance_suite.statement: Support leads can see aging and blocked queue segments from the main dashboard route.
acceptance_suite.verification: Run browser proof against the dashboard route and inspect the screenshot artifact.

acceptance_suite.statement: Risk scoring sorts blocked and SLA-near tickets above normal tickets.
acceptance_suite.verification: Run the risk scoring unit test with seeded ticket fixtures.

acceptance_suite.statement: The final handoff tells the operator how to run, verify, and roll back the dashboard.
acceptance_suite.verification: Read the final delivery packet and match it to the definition of done.

trust_model.authn: Use the host product identity provider or signed internal access for the first slice.
trust_model.authz: Default to read-only support lead and admin roles with no anonymous access.
trust_model.data_policy: Use internal ticket metadata only and exclude customer message bodies from logs and screenshots.
trust_model.privacy: Seeded demos redact names, emails, and free-text customer content.
trust_model.security: No secrets in client code, no write actions in the first release, and dependency checks before ship.
trust_model.auditability: Verification reports cite command output, screenshots, and accepted cuts.

operating_model.observability: Track dashboard load, queue freshness, risk-calculation failures, and error-state rate.
operating_model.support: Support operations owns first-line usage questions with engineering escalation for defects.
operating_model.rollback: Disable the dashboard route or revert the deployment while keeping source ticketing intact.
operating_model.incident_response: Owner reviews failed freshness checks within one business day and records the action.
operating_model.ownership: Support operations owns business rules and engineering owns implementation health.

quality_bar.must_feel_like: A calm operations command center built for fast morning decisions.
quality_bar.must_not_feel_like: A generic chart dump, admin template, or demo with fake confidence.
quality_bar.reference_quality: Decision-grade dashboards from mature support platforms, adapted to the narrow first slice.
quality_bar.concreteness_floor: Every claim maps to a user, surface, acceptance criterion, and proof command.

explicit_cuts.reason: Read-only insight proves the operating value before changing source workflows.
explicit_cuts.risk: Leads still update ticket ownership in the source system for this release.
explicit_cuts.review_trigger: Revisit after two weekly reviews show dashboard-driven unblock actions.
